# 12306 railway travel

A railway ticketing system for searching trains, managing traveler information, booking journeys, and paying for tickets.

Dates and times use Asia/Shanghai. The application, client, server and evaluator start at 2026-07-21T00:00:00+08:00; client and server clocks advance together with elapsed time.

## REQ-1 Public entry

Public entry capability.

Action controls are buttons, navigation destinations are links, and choice controls expose combobox, radio, or checkbox semantics as declared. Selected tabs expose selected state. Forms have associated labels and retain source placeholders; visible collections contain only current results.

**Type:** FOLDER
**Dependencies:** None

### REQ-1.1 Explore homepage and banner carousel

The default landing page shows a 12306 logo on the left and "Login"(role=link), "Register"(role=link), and "My 12306"(role=link) on the right. Navigation offers "Home"(role=link), "Booking"(role=link), and "Travel guide"(role=link), with dropdown entries where specified. "Home banners"(role=region) initially shows Banner 1; "Next banner"(role=button) displays Banner 2 and then Banner 3. Images expose those names; source assets/logo.png and assets/banner1.jpg through banner3.jpg describe visual roles without mandating network URLs. "Ticket search"(role=region) contains "From"(role=textbox) and "To"(role=textbox) with their source placeholders, "Date"(role=textbox), and "Search"(role=button). "Quick Guide"(role=region) supplies quick links including How to book tickets online? and More.

Action controls are buttons, navigation destinations are links, and choice controls expose combobox, radio, or checkbox semantics as declared. Selected tabs expose selected state. Forms have associated labels and retain source placeholders; visible collections contain only current results.

Client and server use Asia/Shanghai, start at 2026-07-21T00:00:00+08:00 and advance together with elapsed time.

## REQ-2 Account access

Account access capability.

**Type:** FOLDER
**Dependencies:** None

### REQ-2.1 Register and validate a traveler account capability

Organize the page-entry and independent user behaviors for Register and validate a traveler account. REQ-2.1.1 establishes the concrete reference pages first; the remaining siblings apply their explicitly preserved source contracts. This abstract capability has no page or executable UI of its own.

For new account: Registration UI; duplicate passport/username records are first created using registration within the same scenario. Source identities are retained in separate case worlds.

**Type:** FOLDER
**Dependencies:** None

#### REQ-2.1.1 Open traveler registration

Follow Register from the public header. Registration displays Nationality, Name, Passport number, Password, Confirm Password, and the Register submit action.

This requirement establishes the page entry and visible reference state before sibling behaviors. It does not implement their validation or state transitions. Every case establishes its own preconditions through the existing UI; tests do not depend on previous cases.

Preserved presentation and source context:
Allow a user to create an account by filling in identity and contact information, agreeing to the service terms, and submitting the registration form.

Open the registration page from the "Register" link in the top-right area of the home page.

Display the registration form with a dropdown labeled "Nationality" showing the default value "Please select" and country options, input fields labeled "Name", "Passport number", "Username", and "Email address", date pickers labeled "Passport expiration date" and "Date of birth", a radio group labeled "Gender" with "Male" and "Female", password fields labeled "Password" and "Confirm Password", a checkbox followed by "I have read and agree to abide by Terms of Service and Privacy Policy of 12306.cn.", and a "Register" button.

The registration form allows a new user to select Nationality "China", enter Name, Passport number, Passport expiration date, Date of birth, Username, Password, Confirm Password, and Email address in labeled controls, select a Gender radio and the agreement checkbox, then activate the "Register" button. A successful submission persists the account and displays "Registration successful.". The passport number and username must be unique.

Reject registration when any required field is missing and show the message "Please fill in all required fields.".

Reject registration when the passport number already exists and show the message "Passport number already exists.". The duplicate-passport scenario first creates the account with passport P20260002 through registration; this is not an additional preloaded duplicate account.

Reject registration when the username already exists and show the message "Username already exists.". The duplicate-username scenario first creates username_taken through registration; this name must not already be occupied in the fresh scenario world.

Reject registration when the values in "Password" and "Confirm Password" do not match and show the message "Passwords do not match.".

Reject registration when the email address format is invalid and show the message "Invalid email address format.".

Reject registration when the agreement checkbox is not selected and show the message "Please agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.".

Initial-world clarification: existing duplicate accounts, extra frequent passengers, and current unpaid/paid/cancelled orders mentioned above are scenario preconditions established through the declared UI creation flows. Only verified accounts and historical completed orders are initially seeded. Source identities, fields and messages remain unchanged.

Confirm Password is a required registration field independently of Password; an empty confirmation uses the missing-required-fields error.

### REQ-2.2 Log in with username email or mobile capability

For authenticated session: Login UI; fresh browser starts logged out.

**Type:** FOLDER
**Dependencies:** None

#### REQ-2.2.1 Open credential login

Follow Login from the public header. The login page displays Email/Username/Mobile number, Password, and LOGIN without authenticating merely by navigation.

This requirement establishes the page entry and visible reference state before sibling behaviors. It does not implement their validation or state transitions. Every case establishes its own preconditions through the existing UI; tests do not depend on previous cases.

Preserved presentation and source context:
Allow a user to log in with a username, email address, or mobile number and a password. The system contains the verified account registered_user with username "registered_user", email "registered_user@example.com", mobile number "13800000010", ID number "P20260010", and password "Password123!".

Open the login page from the "Login" link in the top-right area of the home page.

Display the login form with an input field whose placeholder is "Email/Username/Mobile number", a password input whose placeholder is "Password", and a "LOGIN" button.

The login form accepts a verified username, email address, or mobile number in its "Email/Username/Mobile number" field and a password in its "Password" field. Activating the "LOGIN" button with valid credentials persists the session, displays a status message containing "Login successful", and exposes a "Sign Out" link. The seeded account "registered_user" has password "Password123!".

Reject login when the account field or password field is empty and show the message "Please enter your username/email/phone number and password.".

Reject login when the entered username, email address, or mobile number does not exist and show the message "User not found.".

Reject login when the password is incorrect and show the message "Incorrect password.".

Provide a link with the text "No account yet? Register now." on the login page and navigate to the registration page after it is clicked.

#### REQ-8.3.3 Confirm an order or return to edit

In the valid confirmation dialog, Confirm submits the selected journey/passenger and opens matching payment details with Order submitted successfully. Edit closes the dialog and returns to the booking form without creating an order.

##### REQ-8.3.3.1 Confirm a selected booking order

In "Please confirm the following information."(role=dialog), "Confirm"(role=button) submits the selected train and passenger and opens payment with matching details and successful-submission feedback. "Edit"(role=button) remains the alternative editing action; the parent capability's full submission contract applies.

Shared source contract (preserved from REQ-8.3):
Provide the buttons "Previous step" and "Place order" on the booking form page. When the user clicks "Place order" with at least one selected passenger and all selected ticket classes still having available tickets, open the "Please confirm the following information." dialog showing the selected train and passenger. The order is submitted only after the user activates "Confirm" in that dialog. A verified account named "booking_submit_user" with password "Password123!" has a selectable passenger and can reach the confirmation dialog for an available booking.

Reject booking submission when no passenger is selected and show the message "Please select at least one passenger.".

Reject booking submission when one selected passenger has a ticket class with no remaining tickets and show the message "Sorry, there are no tickets available for the selected ticket class.".

Provide order confirmation, payment, and order status transitions. The seeded accounts each have password "Password123!" and separate passengers named "Passenger Example": booking_confirm_user/P20269991, booking_edit_user/P20269992, booking_payment_user/P20269993, booking_cancel_user/P20269994, booking_paid_user/P20269995, booking_unpaid_user/P20269990, booking_upcoming_user/P20269989, and booking_cancelled_user/P20269988. Orders in these booking flows are created by the scenario actions, not preseeded.

After the user submits booking information, open a confirmation dialog with the title "Please confirm the following information.", show the train information and passenger information, and provide the buttons "Confirm" and "Edit". Clicking "Confirm" confirms the order information and shows a successful submission message. Clicking "Edit" returns to the booking information page.  Separate verified accounts named "booking_confirm_user" and "booking_edit_user", each with password "Password123!", have a selectable frequent passenger and can book an available Shanghai-to-Beijing train.

Initial-world clarification: existing duplicate accounts, extra frequent passengers, and current unpaid/paid/cancelled orders mentioned above are scenario preconditions established through the declared UI creation flows.
